newsitem.title: USA: Higher education seen helping Conn. economy.
newsitem.headline: Higher education seen helping Conn. economy.

text.p: Independent higher education pumped $3.5 billion into Connecticut's economy in fiscal year 1996, according to a study released on Wednesday.

Some $1.5 billion was from direct institutional, student and visitor spending, while $2 billion was from indirect spending, said the study commissioned by the Connecticut Independent College and University Institute for Research and Public Service.
The state's 17 independent institutions created a total of 51,078 jobs, which collectively provided $1.7 billion in employee earnings and $144 million in state and local tax revenues, the study said.
The University of Hartford has a $284 million economic impact and generates 3,683 jobs in the state, the study said.
The researchers said that based on their findings, they will urge increased state investment in higher education to maximize its economic potential.
